cor.heading: Cost of Revenues
cor.text:
Cost of revenues was $4.3 million and $11.6 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to $3.4 million and $10.4 million for the comparable periods of 2025. Cost of revenues accounted for 15% and 14% of our total revenues for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to 12% and 13% for the comparable periods of 2025. The increase for the third quarter of 2026 primarily reflected higher salaries and employee-related costs, higher service costs and customization work for our customers, and higher payments to the Israeli Innovation Authority of the Ministry of Economy and Industry in Israel (the “IIA”). The increase for the first nine months of 2026 primarily reflected higher salaries and employee-related costs and higher payments to the IIA. Included in cost of revenues for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 was a non-cash equity-based compensation expense of $0.2 million and $0.5 million, respectively, as compared to $0.2 million and $0.5 million for the comparable periods of 2025. Gross margin was 85% and 86% for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to 88% and 87% for the comparable periods of 2025.

The number of technical support personnel was 34 at September 30, 2026, as compared to 31 at September 30, 2025.

opex.heading: Operating Expenses
opex.text: Total operating expenses were $28.3 million and $84.2 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to $27.1 million and $78.8 million for the comparable periods of 2025. The net increase for the third quarter of 2026 was primarily due to deal-related costs associated with a potential transaction that was ultimately not consummated and higher salaries and employee-related costs. The net increase for the first nine months of 2026 principally reflected higher salaries and employee-related costs, mainly associated with higher currency exchange expenses as a result of the devaluation of the U.S. dollar against the NIS, and higher non-cash equity-based compensation expenses.

costs.heading: Operating Expenses
costs.text: Total operating expenses were $28.3 million and $84.2 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to $27.1 million and $78.8 million for the comparable periods of 2025. The net increase for the third quarter of 2026 was primarily due to deal-related costs associated with a potential transaction that was ultimately not consummated and higher salaries and employee-related costs. The net increase for the first nine months of 2026 principally reflected higher salaries and employee-related costs, mainly associated with higher currency exchange expenses as a result of the devaluation of the U.S. dollar against the NIS, and higher non-cash equity-based compensation expenses.

rd.heading: Research and Development Expenses, Net
rd.text: Total research and development expenses, net were $18.1 million and $57.3 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to $19.5 million and $55.9 million for the comparable periods of 2025. The decrease for the third quarter of 2026 was primarily due to R&D tax credits recognized under the Crédit Impôt Recherche (the “CIR”) and the new Israeli Law for the Encouragement and Incentivization of Research and Development, 2026 (the “R&D Law”), with the latter reducing research and development expenses in 2026 and having no comparable benefit in 2025, as well as lower non-cash equity-based compensation expenses. The increase for the first nine months of 2026 principally reflected higher salaries and employee-related costs, mainly associated with higher currency exchange expenses as a result of the devaluation of the U.S. dollar against the NIS, partially offset by the tax credits recognized under the R&D Law, which reduced research and development expenses in 2026, with no comparable benefit in 2025. Included in research and development expenses for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 were non-cash equity-based compensation expenses of $2.1 million and $7.7 million, respectively, as compared to $2.6 million and $7.8 million for the comparable periods of 2025.

sm.heading: Sales and Marketing Expenses
sm.text:
Our sales and marketing expenses were $3.9 million and $11.0 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to $3.0 million and $9.8 million for the comparable periods of 2025. The increase for the third quarter of 2026 principally reflected higher salaries and employee-related costs, higher marketing and trade show expenses, and higher non-cash equity-based compensation expenses. The increase for the first nine months of 2026 principally reflected higher commission expenses, higher non-cash equity-based compensation expenses and the cost of a global sales meeting held during the period (an event that did not take place in the first nine months of 2025). Included in sales and marketing expenses for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 were non-cash equity-based compensation expenses of $0.9 million and $2.3 million, respectively, as compared to $0.6 million and $1.7 million for the comparable periods of 2025. Sales and marketing expenses as a percentage of our total revenues were 14% and 13% for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to 11% and 12% for the comparable periods of 2025.

The total number of sales and marketing personnel was 29 at September 30, 2026, as compared to 32 at September 30, 2025.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text:
Our general and administrative expenses were $6.2 million and $15.6 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to $4.4 million and $12.7 million for the comparable periods of 2025. The increase for the third quarter of 2026 was primarily due to deal-related costs associated with a potential transaction that was ultimately not consummated and higher non-cash equity-based compensation expenses. The increase for the first nine months of 2026 was primarily due to deal-related costs associated with a potential transaction that was ultimately not consummated, higher salaries and employee-related costs and higher non-cash equity-based compensation expenses. Included in general and administrative expenses for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 were non-cash equity-based compensation expenses of $1.8 million and $5.0 million, respectively, as compared to $1.5 million and $4.1 million for the comparable periods of 2025. General and administrative expenses as a percentage of our total revenues were 21% and 18% for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to 15% and 16% for the comparable periods of 2025.

The number of general and administrative personnel was 50 at September 30, 2026, as compared to 49 at September 30, 2025.

prov.text: We believe that the assumptions and estimates associated with revenue recognition, equity-based compensation and credit losses have the greatest potential impact on our consolidated financial statements. Therefore, we consider these to be our critical accounting policies and estimates.

net.text: Net cash provided by operating activities for the first nine months of 2026 was $2.5 million and consisted of net loss of $9.7 million, adjustments for non-cash items of $19.1 million, and changes in operating assets and liabilities of $6.9 million. Adjustments for non-cash items primarily consisted of $2.5 million of depreciation and amortization of intangible assets, $15.5 million of equity-based compensation expenses, and $1.3 million of unrealized foreign exchange loss. The decrease in operating assets and liabilities primarily consisted of an increase in prepaid expenses and other assets of $6.7 million (mainly as a result of payment of a yearly design tool subscription, an increase in French research tax benefits applicable to the CIR, advance tax payments, and a $2.6 million increase in unbilled receivables classified as “other long-term assets” in the interim condensed consolidated balance sheets), as well as a decrease in trade payables of $1.2 million and a decrease in accrued payroll and related benefits of $2.4 million (mainly as a result of yearly bonus payments), partially offset by a decrease in trade receivables, net, of $2.7 million and a decrease in operating lease right-of-use assets of $0.8 million.

The decrease in operating assets and liabilities primarily consisted of an increase in prepaid expenses and other assets of $6.7 million (mainly as a result of payment of a yearly design tool subscription, an increase in French research tax benefits applicable to the CIR, advance tax payments, and a $2.6 million increase in unbilled receivables classified as “other long-term assets” in the interim condensed consolidated balance sheets), as well as a decrease in trade payables of $1.2 million and a decrease in accrued payroll and related benefits of $2.4 million (mainly as a result of yearly bonus payments), partially offset by a decrease in trade receivables, net, of $2.7 million and a decrease in operating lease right-of-use assets of $0.8 million.

net sales.heading: Total Revenues
net sales.text:
Total revenues were $29.1 million and $85.1 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, representing an increase of 2% and 9%, as compared to the corresponding periods in 2025. The increase in total revenues for both the third quarter and first nine months of 2026 was primarily attributable to higher licensing and related revenues and royalty revenues, as further described below.

Our five largest customers accounted for 44% and 36% of our total revenues for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to 45% and 39%, respectively, for the comparable periods in 2025. One customer accounted for 11% of our total revenues for the third quarter of 2026, as compared to three customers that each accounted for 11% of our total revenues for the third quarter of 2025. One customer accounted for 10% of our total revenues for the first nine months of 2026, as compared to one customer that accounted for 15% of our total revenues for the first nine months of 2025. Generally, the identity of our customers representing 10% or more of our total revenues varies from period to period, especially with respect to our IP licensing customers, as we generate licensing revenues from new customers on a quarterly basis.

License.text: We license our portfolio of wireless communications, sensing and scalable Edge AI IP to our customers, breaking down barriers to entry and enabling them to bring new cutting-edge products to market faster, more reliably, efficiently and economically.

Royalty.heading: Royalty Revenues
Royalty.text:
Royalty revenues were $12.7 million and $32.7 million for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, representing an increase of 3% and 2% as compared to the corresponding periods in 2025. Royalty revenues accounted for 44% and 38% of our total revenues for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, as compared to 44% and 41% for the comparable periods of 2025. We reported shipments of 623 million Ceva-powered devices in the third quarter of 2026, matching our all-time quarterly record. Our IoT unit volumes reflect the scale and penetration of our connectivity business, with strong Bluetooth volumes, record cellular IoT shipments and record Wi-Fi 6 unit shipments, which carry higher royalty value. This strength was partly offset by weakness in the broader compute-intensive consumer markets, including smartphones, PCs and TVs, where memory market headwinds weighed on demand.

A key development was the continued ramp of internally developed modems at a major U.S. customer, contributing to growth in mobile royalties. This is the first time our customer has moved its internally developed modems into high-volume production across its mainstream flagship smartphone models, an important step for Ceva in this market.

intro.text: Ceva powers the Smart Edge, bridging the digital and physical worlds to bring AI-driven products to life. Our Ceva AI fabric portfolio of silicon and software IP enables devices to Connect, Sense, and Infer – the essential capabilities for the intelligent edge. From 5G , cellular IoT, Bluetooth , Wi-Fi , and UWB connectivity to scalable Edge AI NPUs, AI DSPs, sensor fusion processors and embedded software, Ceva provides the foundational IP for devices that connect, understand their environment, and act in real time. With more than 21 billion devices shipped and trusted by 400+ customers worldwide, Ceva is the backbone of today’s most advanced smart edge products - from AI-infused wearables and IoT devices to autonomous vehicles and 5G infrastructure.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: Customers based in Europe and the Middle East (EME) and Asia Pacific (APAC) accounted for 82% of our total revenues for 2025 and 81% of our total revenues for 2024, with customers in China accounting for 62% and 49% of total revenues for 2025 and 2024, respectively.
Sales to UNISOC (formerly Spreadtrum Communications, Inc.), accounted for 15% and 15% of our total revenues for 2025 and 2024, respectively.

With respect to our royalty revenues in particular, a small number of customers ship substantial volumes of products and thus pay outsized royalty revenues, with two royalty paying customers each representing 10% or more of our total royalty revenues for 2025, and collectively representing 39% of our total royalty revenues for 2025.
Two royalty paying customers each representing 10% or more of our total royalty revenues for 2024, and collectively representing 46% of our total royalty revenues for 2024.
Approximately 82% of our total revenues for 2025 and 81% for 2024 were derived from customers located outside of the United States.

Revenues from customers located in the Asia Pacific (APAC) region account for a substantial portion of these revenues, with significant concentration of revenues in China, which accounted for 62% and 49% of total revenues for 2025 and 2024, respectively.
Sales to UNISOC represented 15% and 15% of our total revenues for 2025 and 2024, respectively.

Generally, the identity of our other customers representing 10% or more of our total revenues varies from period to period, especially with respect to our licensing customers as we generate licensing revenues generally from new customers on a quarterly basis.

With respect to our royalty revenues, two royalty paying customers each represented 10% or more of our total royalty revenues for 2025, and collectively represented 39% of our total royalty revenues for 2025.
Two royalty paying customers each represented 10% or more of our total royalty revenues for 2024, and collectively represented 46% of our total royalty revenues for 2024.
Licensing and related revenue accounted for 58.0% of our total revenues for 2025, compared with 56.1% of our total revenues for 2024.
The five largest royalty-paying customers accounted for 57% of our total royalty revenues for 2025, compared to 61% of our total royalty revenues for 2024.

Because these domains require deep specialization and long development cycles, customers increasingly rely on us to supply the underlying connectivity, sensing, and inference technologies rather than dedicating internal R&D resources to building and maintaining these capabilities themselves.
We rely on a combination of patent, trademark, trade secret and copyright laws and contractual restrictions to protect the proprietary aspects of our technology.
We also rely on trademark, copyright and trade secret laws to protect our IP.
As a result, we rely on our customers to incorporate our technology into their end products at the design stage.
We depend on market acceptance of third-party semiconductor intellectual property.

Our future growth will depend on the level of market acceptance of our third-party licensable IP model, the variety of IP offerings available on the market, and a shift in customer preference away from in-house development of proprietary signal processing IP or AI IPs towards licensing open signal processing IP cores and platforms and AI IPs.
Significant portions of our anticipated future revenues, therefore, will likely depend upon our success in attracting new customers or expanding our relationships with existing customers.

Our ability to succeed in our licensing efforts will depend on a variety of factors, including the performance, quality, breadth and depth of our current and future product portfolio as well as our sales and marketing skills.
Our success will depend on our ability to successfully manage our geographically dispersed operations.

We face a highly competitive employment market and depend on a limited number of key personnel who would be difficult to replace, and changes in our management and sales teams may adversely affect our operations.

We rely on a combination of patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, mask work and other IP rights, confidentiality procedures and IP licensing arrangements to establish and protect our proprietary rights.

We rely on computer systems, hardware, software, technology infrastructure and online sites and networks for both internal and external operations that are critical to our business (collectively, “IT Systems”).
We own and manage some of these IT Systems but also rely on third parties for a range of IT Systems and related products and services.

Our license agreements generally obligate our licensees to pay us a specified royalty for every product they ship that incorporates our technologies, and we rely on our licensees to report their shipments accurately.
Our primary sources of cash inflows are receipts from our accounts receivable, and to some extent interest earned from our cash, deposits and marketable securities.
